scope: Permanent in-frame provenance labels for the DROID first-person to third-person demos
summary: All three task videos and the ten-second reel now identify the wrist stream as REAL CONDITION, both exterior streams as REAL TARGETS, and the absent learned result as OUR GENERATED VIDEO: NOT AVAILABLE / NOT STARTED.
evidence: A transparent 1280x720 SVG overlay permanently labels the left panel REAL CONDITION / FIRST-PERSON and the middle/right panels REAL TARGET A/B / THIRD-PERSON.
Every frame footer states OUR GENERATED VIDEO: NOT AVAILABLE / NOT STARTED; the comparison and labels are PhiAgent-authored, but no novel-view pixels are claimed as generated.
The labeled duck-to-pot, block-to-bowl, and close-drawer outputs decode to 92, 144, and 100 frames at 1280x720 and 15 FPS; the labeled reel decodes to 150 frames and exactly 10 seconds.
The published poster was visually inspected at full resolution and shows all three panel labels plus the generated-video status without covering task pixels.
Manifest schema 2.0.0 records the condition, target, composition, generated-video status, new hashes, and the preserved claim boundary.
lessons: Real condition, real ground-truth target, and model output are three distinct roles and should be labeled inside the video rather than only explained in surrounding prose.
When no learned output exists, an explicit NOT AVAILABLE label is more honest than visually implying that a synchronized target was generated.
limitations: There is still no model-generated ego-to-third-person video; learned generation remains NOT STARTED.
The revision changes labeling and packaging only, not the underlying synchronized DROID pixels or task coverage.
next_actions: Add a separate OUR GENERATED VIDEO panel only after a trained model has produced a held-out result and passed identity, object, temporal, and action gates.
